title: Etale source-and-target locality for the five scheme properties
statement: For schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $P$ be any one of smooth, etale, flat, locally of finite presentation, or locally of finite type, with the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A property $P$ of scheme morphisms is etale local on source-and-target if (i) precomposing a map having $P$ with an etale map preserves $P$; (ii) etale base change preserves $P$; and (iii) a scheme map $f:X\to Y$ has $P$ if and only if, for every $x\in X$, there are schemes $U,V$, etale maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, a point $u\in U$ with $a(u)=x$, and a map $h:U\to V$ with $fa=bh$ and $P(h)$. Each of these five properties is etale local on source-and-target. In particular, in any commutative square $fa=bh$ of schemes with $a:U\to X$ and $b:V\to Y$ etale, $P(f)$ implies $P(h)$; if $a$ is surjective, $P(h)$ implies $P(f)$. For any jointly surjective set-indexed family of etale scheme maps $a_i:U_i\to X$, one has $P(f)$ if and only if $P(fa_i)$ for every $i$. Jointly surjective means that every point of $X$ is in the image of some $a_i$. The empty family is allowed when $X$ is empty. No Noetherian, separation or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Mathlib supplies composition of smooth, etale, flat, locally finitely presented and locally finite type morphisms, and every etale morphism has each of these properties. Thus for the chosen P, infer IsStableUnderComposition P and etale ≤ P. Open immersions, including identity maps, are etale. These facts give precomposition and postcomposition by etale maps.

proof.text: Infer arbitrary base-change stability of P from the existing Mathlib instances for each of the five cases. In particular, P(f) gives P(pullback.snd f b) for any b, and etaleness of b gives etaleness of pullback.fst f b.

source.place: Tags 04QZ, 04R1 and 04R3; singleton source descent and open-image refinement

proof.text: Establish singleton source descent for any surjective etale a:U→X. For smoothness and local finite presentation, use the given family equivalences with the Unit-indexed family constantly equal to a. Use Etale.of_comp_of_surjective_etale for etaleness, the already proved source-library Flat.of_comp_of_flat_of_surjective for flatness, and locallyOfFiniteType_of_flat_lfp_source for local finite type. Etale a supplies the required flatness and local finite presentation. No quasi-compactness is needed.

source.place: Tags 04QZ, 04R1 and 04R3; singleton source descent and open-image refinement

proof.text: For any jointly surjective etale family a_i:U_i→X, let W_i be its open image. Factor a_i as q_i followed by W_i→X, using IsOpenImmersion.lift. Etale cancellation makes q_i etale; injectivity of W_i→X and the definition of its image make q_i surjective. From P(a_i followed by f), singleton descent gives P(f restricted to W_i). The W_i cover X, so IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_iSup_eq_top gives P(f); the converse is composition. The five source-local instances come from their affine-local ring-hom definitions. The index may lie in any universe: no coproduct is formed. An empty family gives an empty open covering and the same Zariski-local criterion.

source.place: Tags 04QZ, 04R1 and 04R3; singleton source descent and open-image refinement

proof.text: Cancel an etale target b:V→Y from h:U→V. Form B=U×_Y V for h followed by b and b, and the graph s=(id_U,h):U→B. The projection B→U is etale, and s followed by that projection is the identity, so etale cancellation makes s etale. The other projection has P by base change of h followed by b; composing with s gives P(h). This graph argument does not require separatedness.

source.place: Tags 04QZ, 04R1 and 04R3; singleton source descent and open-image refinement

proof.text: For a commutative square a followed by f = h followed by b, composition with a and target cancellation give P(f)→P(h). Conversely compose h with b and descend along the surjective etale a. For the pointwise criterion, use identity charts in the forward direction. Conversely choose one chart and lift above each x in X. These source charts are jointly surjective, and their composites with f have P by postcomposition with the etale target charts. Apply family descent. Combine with precomposition and base-change stability to obtain all clauses.
